memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it is to consist of the finest flour: either thick loaves made without yeast and with olive oil mixed in or thin loaves made without yeast and brushed with olive oil.'" - Lev 2:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God allows variety. The offering could be raw flour, or it could be baked. Thick loaves or thin. Oil mixed in or brushed on top. Different households, different ovens, different hands — and God accepted them all.

But within that freedom, one thing is fixed: without yeast.

In Scripture yeast usually pictures something that spreads quietly through the whole batch — most often corruption or hypocrisy. Jesus warned His disciples about the yeast of the Pharisees (Lk 12:1). Paul told the Corinthians that a little yeast works through the whole batch of dough, and urged them to get rid of the old yeast of malice and wickedness (1 Cor 5:6-8).

So here is the balance God sets. He gives real freedom in the form of our worship — there is no single approved recipe, no one correct style, no exclusive method. But He is not indifferent to what quietly ferments inside it.

We often get this backwards. We argue fiercely about the outward form of worship and pay little attention to the resentment, pride, or pretence rising invisibly in the dough.

God looks at what is in the loaf.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I more concerned with the style of my worship than the state of my heart in it?
2. Is there any quiet "yeast" — pretence, bitterness, hidden compromise — working through me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, search what is rising unseen in me. Give me freedom in how I worship You and purity in why I do. Amen.
